title: Blood Relations

steps.title: Understanding Family Trees
steps.content: Blood relation problems ask you to determine the relationship between two people based on given information. Draw a family tree diagram to visualize relationships.
steps.example: If A is B's father and B is C's mother, then A is C's grandfather.
steps.tip: Use standard symbols: M for male, F for female, ← for parent-child. Start from the youngest generation and work upward.

steps.title: Identify the Relationship
steps.prompt: A man points to a girl and says: “She is the daughter of my father's only son.” How is the girl related to the man?
steps.explanation: The man's father's only son is the man himself. The girl is his daughter.
hints: Start from the person named after 'my' or 'his/her' and draw one relationship at a time.
Do not jump generations: parent, sibling and child links must stay explicit.

steps.title: Quick Practice
steps.prompt: A is B's brother. C is A's father. D is C's father. How is D related to B?
steps.explanation: C is B's father (since A is B's brother). D is C's father, so D is B's grandfather.
hints: Draw the family tree from the speaker's point of view.
Follow the chain one link at a time, then name the final person's relation to the requested person.

steps.title: Common Relationship Chains
steps.content: Learn these common chains: Father's father → Grandfather, Father's mother → Grandmother, Mother's father → Maternal grandfather, Father's brother → Uncle, Father's sister → Aunt.
steps.tip: For complex chains, break them down: Person X → relation Y → relation Z → target person.

steps.title: Complex Chain
steps.prompt: A's mother is the sister of B. B's father is the son of C. Assuming the siblings share both parents, how is C related to A?
steps.explanation: B's father is also A's mother's father. That man is C's son, so C is one generation above A's maternal grandfather: A's great-grandparent.
hints: Mark each person's gender only when the sentence provides it.
Trace the chain from the final named person back to the person asked about.

questions.prompt: A man says: “The lady is the daughter of my father's only son.” How is the lady related to the man?
questions.explanation: The man's father's only son is the man himself. The lady is his daughter.

questions.prompt: A is the father of B. B is the sister of C. C is the brother of D. How is D related to A?
questions.explanation: B, C, and D are all children of A. B is female, C is male. D's gender is not specified, so D is A's child (son or daughter).

questions.prompt: Anu is Bala's mother. Bala is Charan's father. How is Anu related to Charan?
questions.explanation: Bala is Charan's father and Anu is Bala's mother, so Anu is Charan's paternal grandmother.

questions.prompt: Ravi is Sita's brother. Sita is Mohan's mother. How is Ravi related to Mohan?
questions.explanation: Sita is Mohan's mother. Her brother Ravi is Mohan's maternal uncle.

questions.prompt: P is Q's daughter. Q is R's son. What is P's relation to R?
questions.explanation: Q is R's son and P is Q's daughter, so P is R's granddaughter.

srs_cards.question: How do you solve blood relation problems systematically?
srs_cards.answer: Draw a family tree. Start from the youngest generation and work upward. Break complex chains into smaller steps.

srs_cards.question: What are the key ideas in Blood Relations?
srs_cards.answer: Translate family statements into relationships. Track gender and generation separately. Draw a family tree for multi-step questions. Avoid assuming unstated relationships.

srs_cards.question: Name a common mistake in Blood Relations.
srs_cards.answer: The statement may describe an in-law; track the exact relationship given.

srs_cards.question: What is the safest way to solve a long blood-relation chain?
srs_cards.answer: Draw a family tree and add one relationship at a time.

learning_objectives: Translate family statements into a family-tree diagram.
Track maternal and paternal relationships across generations.
Use gender information without assuming unstated facts.
Solve multi-step family relationship questions accurately.

common_misconceptions.misconception: A sibling of a parent is always an uncle regardless of gender.
common_misconceptions.correction: A parent's brother is an uncle and a parent's sister is an aunt; use the gender clue.

common_misconceptions.misconception: The speaker's gender can be assumed from the sentence.
common_misconceptions.correction: Use only explicit gender information; otherwise the relationship may remain gender-neutral.

common_misconceptions.misconception: A relationship chain should be read only from left to right.
common_misconceptions.correction: Anchor the reference person first and trace each pronoun to the person it refers to.

worked_examples.title: Follow two relationships
worked_examples.input: A is B's mother. B is C's brother.
trace: A is one generation above B.
worked_examples.explanation: Represent each relation as an edge in a small family tree.

worked_examples.title: Track paternal relation
worked_examples.input: P is the father of Q. Q is the sister of R.
trace: Q and R share sibling relation.
P is also the father of R.
worked_examples.explanation: Sibling relationships connect the same parent group when the question establishes it.

worked_examples.title: Avoid unsupported assumptions
trace: It does not specify which parent is related.
It does not specify gender or age.
worked_examples.explanation: A correct answer uses only the facts provided.

company_applications.practice: Sketch each generation and mark genders explicitly.
Translate pronouns into a diagram before selecting an option.
Avoid assuming relationships that are not stated.

quest.story: A set of family statements has arrived in the hiring arena. Your task is to turn each statement into a family tree so the relationship is proven rather than guessed.
quest.mission: Track generations, gender clues and family links using a small diagram.
success_criteria: Identify the reference person in a statement.
Draw parent, child and sibling links.
